name: Malian Tiguadege Na (Peanut Stew)
description: Tiguadege na, meat stewed in a rich ground peanut sauce, is widely considered Mali's national dish, built on real ground peanuts rather than a generic nut butter substitute.
steps_detailed: Brown the chicken with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter with the tomatoes and a little water, then add to the pot.
Simmer 25-28 minutes until the chicken is very tender.

name: Malian Jollof Rice
description: Jollof rice, tomato-and-pepper rice cooked until it takes on real color and depth, is beloved across Mali as it is throughout much of West Africa.
steps_detailed: Blend the tomatoes, bell pepper, and half the onion into a smooth puree.
Brown the chicken, 6-7 minutes, then set aside.
Fry the remaining onion, add the tomato paste, cook 2 minutes, then add the puree and simmer uncovered 15-18 minutes until deeply reduced.
Stir in the rice, broth, and chicken, cover, and cook on low 20-25 minutes until tender.

name: Malian Fonio Porridge
description: Fonio, an ancient grain domesticated in West Africa and long central to Malian farming, used here in a simple breakfast porridge - fonio itself isn't a distinct item here, so this leans on the closest widely available small grain instead.
steps_detailed: Simmer the couscous with the milk and honey 8-10 minutes until soft and creamy.
steps: Simmer the couscous with the milk and honey 8-10 minutes until soft and creamy.

name: Malian Riz Gras
description: Riz gras, meaning 'fat rice', a rich tomato-and-meat rice dish, a common Malian one-pot meal shared across much of West Africa.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef, 6-7 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and carrot, and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the rice and 1.25 cups water, cover, and simmer 18-20 minutes until tender.

name: Malian Poulet Yassa
description: Yassa, chicken marinated and cooked in a mountain of caramelized onions and lemon, is beloved across Mali as it is throughout the wider Senegambian region.
steps_detailed: Marinate the chicken in the lemon juice and garlic for at least 20 minutes.
Brown the chicken, 6-7 minutes, then set aside.
Cook the onion over medium-low heat, stirring often, 20-25 minutes, until deeply softened and sweet.
Return the chicken with a splash of water and simmer 15 minutes more.
